plan.title: bug(test,windows): the --with-network session:start case makes a real npm registry request under a 20s budget and is load-flaky

narratives.Description: Make `session:start --with-network probes only the disclosed public npm registry` deterministic by replacing its pass-through `spawnSync` spy with a command-selective stub and by injecting the deep SCM probe, so the case performs no outbound request while the #2182 argv assertion stays exact. Remove the local `timeout: 20_000` override that contradicts the recorded win32 policy in `vitest.config.ts:210-225`, and add two mutation checks plus a control that make the hermetic claim falsifiable.
narratives.Overview:
Two independent causes, both addressed.

Cause 1 -- the mock is a pass-through spy. `vi.mock("node:child_process")` returns `spawnSync: vi.fn(actual.spawnSync)`, which records AND executes, so the case really runs `npm view @deftai/directive version --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ --ignore-scripts`. The production path is `probeSessionReleaseAvailability` -> `packages/core/src/session/release-availability.ts:47-59` (`defaultNpmView`, `timeout: 5_000`), NOT `doctor/payload-staleness.ts` (15 s). The file header's attribution is wrong.

Cause 2 -- the case overrides the win32 timeout policy. `vitest.config.ts:210-225` sets `testTimeout: 120_000` on win32 and records that a git-fixture test issuing 10-30 sequential spawns takes 25-80 s. This case overrides that to `timeout: 20_000` while `initPrivateScopeRepo` runs six sequential git subprocesses. That cause survives any network fix.

Implementation shape is bound by the design critique: use the low-level command-selective stub pattern from `packages/core/src/doctor/npm-view.test.ts` -- stub npm/pnpm command execution, return a well-shaped deterministic process result, keep the exact singleton argv assertion. A high-level `probeReleaseAvailability` injection is forbidden here because it bypasses construction of the security-relevant argv and weakens #2182.

Scope decision on criterion 1: take the STRONGER claim. `probeScm` is already a first-class injectable seam on `SessionStartOptions` (`session-start.ts:307`), and `allowOptionalNetwork: true` selects `depth: "deep"`, whose runner spawns live `gh` on a 30-second subprocess timeout (`scm/readiness.ts:285-315`). Leaving it live would satisfy the narrow npm/pnpm form of criterion 1 while preserving both an outbound request and a second wall-clock hazard that criteria 3 and 4 exist to remove. The control test therefore asserts that no network-capable command is executed at all.

items.title: The --with-network case issues no npm or pnpm network request, and the stronger no-outbound-request claim is taken: the SCM probe is injected and a control test establishes it
The assertion still fails when a flow contacts the private-scope registry and still fails when the public-registry probe is dropped, as two explicit mutation checks
The local timeout: 20_000 override is removed so the case inherits the vitest.config.ts win32 policy
A deterministic no-registry control is the gate-worthy evidence, and the repeated-run smoke check names an exact command with an explicit concurrency and load shape
The file header names the session release-availability seam and no longer claims a stub where a pass-through spy was used
No real-network test remains in this suite; the executed-passthrough allowlist is the marker that keeps it that way

missing_traces_justification: file_scope deliberately undeclared: verify:scope-provenance fails closed on a declared file_scope without an operator-minted base-approved digest that a worker cannot obtain (#3874).
Partitioning spawn-heavy suites into their own vitest project is the next step named in vitest.config.ts:222-224 and is out of scope here.
Hook-runtime travel (#3785) and the orphan-active work on #3893 are owned by other sessions and are not touched.

intended_placement.cohesion_exemption: Test-only change inside the suite that owns the assertion, plus the release-notes entry. No production source moves.
